new_statements.rule_in_words: KiLega is described as tonal (lexical/grammatical H vs L with derived rising and falling contours); the dissertation contains no statement about word stress or accent placement (verified by full-text search-within: accent, syllable, penultimate, lengthening, prosodic = 0 hits). For the sister variety Beya Lega (lega1249) Botne 2003:425-427 adds phrase-final penultimate vowel lengthening (blocked by a final H) and likewise uses no stress/accent notion; no source transfers this to Isile/Lega-Mwenga.
new_statements.exceptions: None (tone only). Botne 2003 (Beya, lega1249): penultimate lengthening fails when the final vowel bears H.
new_statements.domain_note: Snippet-level access only; the tone remark is an aside in a syntax thesis, not a phonology chapter. Kinyalolo 1991:10 distinguishes a Mwenga ('Ntata/East') dialect from Shabunda and Pangi ('Malinga/West'); which dialect his own data represent could not be verified from snippets, although Glottolog files the thesis under lega1250.
new_statements.identity_note: lega1250 = Lega-Mwenga, i.e. Isile/Kisile/Ishile ('Lega-Ntara'; Kinyalolo 1991:10 'Mwenga.. Ntata (East) dialect'), the eastern Lega variety of Mwenga territory, South Kivu. All accessible Lega phonology is for OTHER varieties: Botne 2003 and Botne 1994 describe Beya (Pangi District) and Meeussen 1962/1971 the Banagabo of Shabunda, both Lega-Malinga = Lega-Shabunda, glottocode lega1249 (Botne 2003:422 gives only c. 67% lexical similarity between Isile and Lega-Malinga), so their prosodic statements (tone language; phrase-final penultimate lengthening) must not be booked under lega1250. Kinyalolo 1991 is filed under lega1250 by Glottolog, but the dialect basis of his data could not be verified from snippets. Glottolog's 'grammar sketch' list for lega1250 is polluted with unrelated EPP/Spec-head syntax papers (Finnish, Basque, Latin etc.); the genuine descriptive items are Kinyalolo 1991, Lungumbu 1988, Itangaza 1993 and unpublished Kisile memoires.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Describes the Beya variety of Pangi District (Lega-Malinga = lega1249, NOT Isile/Lega-Mwenga; p.422 puts Isile vs Lega-Malinga at c. 67% lexical similarity). p.425 sect. 2.4: 'Vowels are lengthened in the penultimate syllable of a word in phrase-final position.. However, if there is a high tone on the final vowel, lengthening does not occur'. pp.426-7 sect. 2.8: 'Lega is a tone language' (H, L distinctive; downstepped H, R, F derived). The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur in the chapter.
